questions.q: Which of these is one of the seven sections of the reusable policy document template?
options: Owner and approver, tied to the RACI matrix
A list of software license costs
The personal phone numbers of committee members
A full technical implementation guide for developers
questions.explain: Owner/approver is one of the seven template sections; implementation detail belongs in a standard, not the policy.

questions.q: In the policy lifecycle, who typically drafts the first version of a policy, and who provides business context?
options: The steward typically drafts it; the owner provides business context
An outside auditor drafts it with no internal input
The sponsor personally writes every policy
No one drafts it — policies are generated automatically
questions.explain: This matches the RACI from Lesson 5: owner Accountable (context), steward Responsible (drafting).

questions.q: Why does the lesson say naming a specific tool or technique inside a policy statement is a mistake?
options: It makes the policy age badly the moment that tool changes — that detail belongs in a standard
Tools should never be mentioned anywhere in governance documentation
It is illegal to name software products in internal documents
Standards are not allowed to reference tools either
questions.explain: Policies should stay implementation-agnostic; naming a specific tool ties the policy's lifespan to that tool's lifespan.

questions.q: What happens to a policy that is never scheduled for a review cadence?
options: It quietly goes stale as the business, regulations, or systems change underneath it
It automatically becomes a standard instead
It is legally voided after one year in every case
Nothing changes — policies never need review once approved
questions.explain: The lesson stresses that a review cadence is what keeps a policy accurate as circumstances change, not an optional nicety.

questions.q: Why is a policy nobody can find functionally equivalent to not having one, according to the lesson?
options: It must be published in a central, discoverable location to actually govern behavior
Policies are only valid if printed on paper
Only the sponsor is allowed to know where policies are stored
Discoverability is not actually mentioned as a requirement
questions.explain: The publish stage of the lifecycle specifically calls for a central, discoverable location — an unfindable policy can't be followed.
